2.w: “Do you think this to be just when you say, ‘My right before God’?

3.w: But you say, ‘What will it profit you,’ and, ‘What do I gain by not sinning?’

4.w: I will reply to you, and to your friends with you.

5.w: Gaze at the heavens and see; consider the clouds, which are higher than you.

6.w: If you sin, how does it affect God? If your transgressions are many, what does it do to him?

7.w: If you are righteous, what do you give to God, or what does he receive from your hand?

8.w: Your wickedness affects only a person like yourself, and your righteousness only other people.

9.w: “People cry out because of the excess of oppression; they cry out for help because of the power of the mighty.

10.w: But no one says, ‘Where is God, my Creator, who gives songs in the night,

11.w: who teaches us more than the wild animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?’

12.w: Then they cry out—but he does not answer— because of the arrogance of the wicked.

13.w: Surely it is an empty cry —God does not hear it; the Almighty does not take notice of it.

14.w: How much less, then, when you say that you do not perceive him, that the case is before him and you are waiting for him!

15.w: And further, when you say that his anger does not punish, and that he does not know transgression!

16.w: So Job opens his mouth to no purpose; without knowledge he multiplies words.”
